original_question: A quasimorphism on a group G is a function f: G → R such that the quantity sup |f(g) + f(h) − f(gh)| is finite. A quasimorphism is homogeneous if it restricts to g,h a homomorphism on every cyclic subgroup of G. Let G be a group admitting an unbounded homogeneous quasimorphism G → R that is not a homomorphism. Must G contain a non-abelian free subgroup?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.48 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of arXiv:1401.0300
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact formulation. It correctly uses a real-valued quasimorphism on a group G, gives the right bounded-defect condition sup_{g,h}|f(g)+f(h)-f(gh)|<infinity, singles out homogeneous quasimorphisms, assumes the existence of an unbounded homogeneous quasimorphism that is not a genuine homomorphism, and asks exactly whether this forces G to contain a non-abelian free subgroup.
missing_details: The homogeneity clause should be cleaned up to read: "it restricts to a homomorphism on every cyclic subgroup of G."
For full stand-alone precision, make explicit that the codomain is R and that "unbounded" means the image f(G) is unbounded in R.
It is worth stating explicitly that the paper imposes no additional hypotheses on G such as finite generation, torsion-freeness, linearity, or countability.
If one wants maximum explicitness, "not a homomorphism" should be read as "not a group homomorphism G -> R."
refined_question: Let G be a group. A function f: G -> R is called a quasimorphism if sup_{g,h in G} |f(g)+f(h)-f(gh)| < infinity. It is called homogeneous if its restriction to every cyclic subgroup of G is a homomorphism. Suppose that G admits an unbounded homogeneous quasimorphism f: G -> R that is not a group homomorphism. Must G contain a non-abelian free subgroup?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of the official open problem 21.48 in the Kourovka Notebook. In this arXiv item, the exact target is not a Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3 cluster from a standard article; rather, arXiv:1401.0300 is the continuously updated Kourovka Notebook, and the matching item is the standalone open problem 21.48. The problem statement itself supplies the relevant definitions of quasimorphism and homogeneous quasimorphism, and there is no narrower reformulation or equivalent version given nearby that should replace it.
